title: Does Moral Code Have a Moral Code? Probing Delphi’s Moral Philosophy

bias_targets.methodology: Probing the model with standardized morality questionnaires, such as the Community, Autonomy, and Divinity Scale (CADS), to demonstrate that the model's judgments disproportionately align with Western, individualistic moral frameworks rather than non-Western ethics focused on community and divinity.

Administering the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) and Oxford Utilitarianism Scale (OUS) to evaluate the model's moral judgments, revealing a strong alignment with liberal moral values (prioritizing Care/Fairness and Impartial Beneficence) over conservative values (Loyalty/Authority/Purity).

Comparing the model's ethical responses on standardized moral scales to demographic data in psychological literature, which shows the model's moral priorities mirror those of younger populations rather than older generations.
